o: "Write a friendly 3 line email to a customer whose order is late. Offer 10% off."
quizzes.why: Details in, quality out. Tell it who, what and how.
It can read images, including handwriting. Double check names and numbers.

quizzes.q: What should you {always} do before sending an AI reply?
quizzes.why: AI drafts. You decide. Read every word before it goes out.

quizzes.q: Is the {free} version of Claude enough to start?
quizzes.why: Free is plenty to learn and do real work. Upgrade only when you hit limits.

o: A chatbot answers. An agent does a task.
quizzes.why: Agents take action, like drafting every reply in your inbox.

quizzes.q: Best way to make AI sound like {you?}
o: Paste examples of how you write
quizzes.why: Show, don't tell. Two real examples beat any description.

quizzes.q: AI stated a fact that's {wrong.} What happened?
quizzes.why: AI can sound sure and still be wrong. Always check facts that matter.

quizzes.q: How long does a Business Brain take to {make?}
quizzes.why: 15 questions, about 5 minutes. Comment BRAIN on any post for the free tool.

polls.q: Would you let AI {draft} your replies?
Do you reply to new leads within {1 hour?}

facts.more: Send it a photo of a confusing bill, an error message or a menu in another language.
facts.try: "What does this mean, and what should I do?"

facts.f: AI can clone a voice from {under a minute} of audio.
facts.more: Scammers use this to fake calls from family. Agree on a code word with yours.
facts.try: Ask a weird personal question only they'd know.

facts.f: Claude can read an entire {contract} in one go.
facts.more: Paste or upload the whole thing and get the parts that matter.
facts.try: "List anything in here that could cost me money."

facts.more: Snap a photo of a whiteboard, a note or an old notebook page.
facts.try: "Type this up and turn it into a to do list."

facts.f: Without web search on, a chatbot {doesn't know today's news.}
facts.more: It only knows what it learned in training, up to a cutoff date.

facts.f: AI can write a spreadsheet formula from {plain English.}
facts.more: No more googling how VLOOKUP works.
facts.try: "Give me a formula that adds column C only when column B says paid."

facts.more: Reply to a customer in Spanish, Portuguese or Korean in seconds.
facts.try: "Reply to this in their language, friendly and short."

facts.f: Claude can build a working {calculator or mini app} from one sentence.
facts.more: No code from you. It writes it and shows it right in the chat.
facts.try: "Build me a quote calculator for my cleaning prices."

facts.f: AI {forgets} your last chat unless you save context.
facts.more: Memory and Projects fix that. Otherwise every chat starts fresh.
facts.try: Save your business info in a Project once.

facts.f: Chatbots don't read words. They read {tokens.}
facts.more: In English, one token is roughly three quarters of a word.

facts.f: AI can sound {100% sure} and still be wrong.
facts.more: It's called a hallucination. It's why you read before you send.
facts.try: "How confident are you? What should I double check?"

facts.f: AI will tell you why your plan {could fail,} if you ask.
facts.more: By default it tends to agree with you. Ask it to push back.

facts.f: AI can turn a {voice note} into a clean email.
facts.more: Talk for a minute, paste the transcript, let it write.
facts.try: "Turn this rambling into a short, clear email."

facts.f: Faces made by AI can look {completely real.}
facts.more: Don't trust a profile picture alone before you send money or info.

facts.f: ChatGPT hit an estimated {100 million users} in about two months.
facts.more: Analysts called it the fastest growing consumer app at the time.

facts.f: In 2016, AI beat the world's best Go player with a move experts called {impossible.}
facts.more: AlphaGo's makers estimated a human would play Move 37 about 1 time in 10,000.

facts.f: AI has predicted the shape of {200 million proteins.}
facts.more: Work that used to take scientists years per protein. It won a Nobel Prize in 2024.

facts.f: The first chatbot was built in {1966.}
facts.more: It was called ELIZA. People confided in it, even though it mostly repeated their words back.
